provenance.text: Provenance: this world is a code-led refinement of the incumbent UI-kit world (`design/secure-messenger-ui-kit.html`, `design/gasapp.tokens.json`) raised to an own world, "intaglio". The concept-seed roll was waived (no seed key) on the owner's explicit brief "можно даже отклониться чуть от UI kit и сделать что то красивее и эффектнее но без лагов и перегрузки" (allowed to deviate a bit from the kit, more beautiful and striking, without lag or overload), with confirmed constraints: keep the kit's dark theme, no "hacker" look, a new palette allowed, Android screens only. No image generation was used, no comps were produced, and no shipping rasters exist: the launcher icon, backgrounds and the seal are XML vectors or code-drawn.

narrative.overview:
GasApp is a security document the person carries, not a terminal. The screens borrow the grammar of intaglio security printing (passports, banknotes): a ground of deep printing inks in tonal steps, fine-line guilloche drawn in hairline strokes, and exactly one luminous ink, periwinkle, reserved for action and for the person's own words. It deliberately refuses the category default of near-black plus a single neon cyan, and refuses the "hacker" register entirely: no terminal green, no glitch, no skulls.

The density is that of a calm, conventional Android messenger: 16dp screen margins, 64-72dp list rows, 48dp touch targets, sp type that scales with the system. The document character lives in three places only: the palette (ink-navy ground, never black), the outgoing speech bubble (periwinkle ink with dark text, "ink on paper"), and the guilloche seal, which appears on four surfaces and nowhere else. Everything else is quiet, so waiting on Tor reads as a normal state rather than a failure.

Motion is short, decelerating and functional: the seal turns one notch per PIN digit, opens on a correct PIN, shakes and flashes red on a wrong one; new messages rise 14dp into place. All of it is skipped when the system has animations removed, and none of it may cost frames on a weak phone.
keyCharacteristics: Deep ink-navy ground in four tonal steps plus a 1dp hairline; no shadows.
One action ink (periwinkle); status inks green / amber / red carry security meaning only.
Code-drawn guilloche rosette as the brand mark, on lock, onboarding welcome, empty chat list and security center only.
Inter for all interface text; monospace for anything a human verifies character by character.
Always dark; the theme never follows system light mode.
Motion skipped entirely when the system disables animations.

rules.name: The One Ink Rule
rules.body: Periwinkle is the only action color. If something is tappable and primary, it is periwinkle; if it is not, it is not periwinkle. No second accent.

rules.name: The Semantic Inks Rule
rules.body: Green means verified, amber means attention, red means error or danger. They never decorate, and avatar inks never include green, amber or red, so a contact's color can never read as a security state.

rules.name: The Navy Not Black Rule
rules.body: The ground is ink-navy (#0E1238) in tonal steps. Pure black appears only as the camera scrim on the QR scanner.

rules.name: The Line-Height-Travels-With-Size Rule
rules.body: Every step is size, line height and weight together (Android `lineSpacingExtra` = token line height minus size). Taking the size alone is how screens look "close but wrong".

rules.name: The Mono For Verification Rule
rules.body: Anything a person compares character by character (safety number, key, recovery key) is set in monospace, and the style sets both the platform and AppCompat font attributes so Inter cannot override it.

rules.name: The Tonal Steps Rule
rules.body: A surface is raised by moving one navy step lighter and adding a hairline, never by a shadow or a glow.

rules.name: The Ink On Paper Rule
rules.body: The person's own words are printed in periwinkle ink with dark text. Outgoing bubbles never use a dim or translucent accent and never use light text on periwinkle.

rules.name: The Four Seals Rule
rules.body: The rosette appears on the lock screen, onboarding welcome, empty chat list and security center, and nowhere else. It is the mark, not a texture.

rules.name: The Still When Asked Rule
rules.body: Every animation (seal turn, open, reject, ink-in, message rise, strip progress) is skipped and jumps to its end state when the system has animations disabled.

dos: **Do** use Periwinkle Ink (#FFCB2E) as the only action color, with On-Ink Navy (#2B1600) text on it.
**Do** raise surfaces by navy tonal steps plus a 1dp Hairline (#343E85) stroke.
**Do** reference spacing, radius and type by token name; keep layouts free of raw numbers.
**Do** keep touch targets at 48dp or larger and all type in sp.
**Do** set safety numbers, keys and recovery keys in monospace.
**Do** show the connection route on the chat list whenever Tor or a proxy is not connected.
**Do** give every status icon (delivery ticks, verification) a spoken label.
**Do** skip all motion when the system disables animations, and run seal movement on a hardware layer.
donts: **Don't** use a "hacker" look: no terminal green, neon cyan on black, glitch, matrix or skull imagery.
**Don't** use pure black as a surface; the ground is Ink Navy (#0E1238).
**Don't** use green, amber or red for anything but their security meaning, and don't add them to avatar inks.
**Don't** place the guilloche seal outside lock, onboarding welcome, empty chat list and security center.
**Don't** add shadows or glows for elevation.
**Don't** follow the system light theme; the app is always dark.
**Don't** show calls, voice, groups or push affordances; the product has none.
**Don't** use Disabled Text (#6670AD) for anything a person must read.
**Don't** add raster imagery or heavy visual libraries; marks and backgrounds are vectors or code-drawn.
